There's plenty of pent-up enthusiasm as this is Milwaukee's first baseball championship

For NPR News, I'm Chuck Humboldt in Milwaukee.
It's NPR.
Iran continues to target ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz.
NPR's Hadil Al-Jalchi reports this comes as the U.S. and Israel prepare, again, for

The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said that in the past 24 hours, three oil

It reported that the vessels were going through a "unauthorized route" and that the ships
caught fire.
There were no reports of casualties.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations, which monitors shipping vessels, said that October had the

Hadil Al-Jalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
It's time to change the time again.
Most people in the U.S. will turn their clocks back an hour this weekend, and Piers Winther
Johnson reports many would rather stop changing them all together.
A new poll by the public research group YouGov finds 63 percent of Americans want to end
the twice-yearly clock changes, but there is disagreement over which time to keep.
42 percent favor permanent daylight saving time, which means more daylight in the evening,
compared with 28 percent who prefer standard time.
The debate over the issue continues in Congress, where legislation has bounced between the
House and Senate for years.
The Senate passed the Sunshine Protection Act in 2022, but it never advanced in the
House.
A newer measure passed the House in July and remains stalled in the Senate amid concerns
over darker mornings during the winter months.
For now, though, clocks fall back an hour early on Sunday.
Winther Johnson, NPR News This is NPR.
